what_it_shows: Business email compromise and payment diversion against commercial clients; account takeover through credential stuffing, phishing kits, adversary-in-the-middle phishing and SIM swap; remote-access scams; ransomware, data theft and destructive attacks on financial institutions; DDoS against bank websites; edge device exploitation; malicious vendor software updates; deepfake voice impersonation; authorized push payment scams on instant payments; card enumeration; ATM skimming and jackpotting; prompt injection against customer-facing generative assistants; sector alerts reviewed daily, with advisories ticketed

title: Records retention schedule
source_system: Records management office
what_it_shows: Security documentation and superseded policy versions kept 7 years; SAR supporting records kept 5 years; payment records retained per the schedule; logs kept 7 years in the archive

title: Productivity suite mail flow, security and conditional access settings
source_system: Productivity suite admin console (SYS-13)
what_it_shows: External sender tags; auto-forward blocking; monitoring and takedown of look-alike domains; email filtering and data loss prevention; conditional access policies; about 640 commercial client service staff exchange payment instructions with clients by email

title: Identity theft red flags program (bank)
source_system: Fraud Strategy files
what_it_shows: Written program under 12 CFR 41.90 approved by the board; red flag rules from CIAM signals (new device, contact data change followed by a payee add); staff changes to customer contact data in the core are not among the monitored red flags; annual report to the board risk committee 2026-02

title: Contact center and telephony records
source_system: Cloud contact center service; telecom records
owner: Head of Consumer and Small Business Banking
what_it_shows: One cloud contact center service for 3 sites, with a backup carrier for inbound numbers; knowledge-based caller authentication for some requests; customer alerts sent to the old contact details after a contact change

title: New product approval records, 2025-04 to 2026-03
source_system: New product approval committee files
what_it_shows: Approvals recorded for new products and services; vendor AI feature releases inside existing SaaS tools do not appear in the approval records

title: Technology investment plan and project charters
source_system: CIO portfolio office
what_it_shows: The 2026 to 2027 project list includes a logically isolated cyber vault for core data planned for 2027, a mainframe connector for identity governance, and the migration of legacy commercial platform clients due 2027-02-26

title: BIA interviews with process owners
source_system: Interviews (Head of Payments Operations; Head of Treasury Management; Head of Core Banking Technology; Head of Consumer and Small Business Banking; Director of Fraud Strategy; Chief Financial Officer; Controller; Head of Consumer Lending; Head of Commercial Banking; BSA/AML Officer; President, Cris Santos Investment Services; Head of Wealth and Institutional Services; Chief Human Resources Officer; Chief Data and Analytics Officer)
what_it_shows: Each owner's description of the process, the systems, third parties and people it uses, its manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the owner says it can tolerate; Payments Operations states that manual sanctions review handles about 400 wires an hour against a peak of 2,500; digital banking states that call volumes triple within 2 hours of an outage; the Controller states that the MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end window

title: BIA dependency, contract and test record review, with observed tests
source_system: Vendor contracts; DR test records; contract RTO schedule
what_it_shows: Contract RTOs, alternates and last test dates for 26 dependencies; 15 are single points of failure and 2 have never been tested by the bank; card processor test observed on 2026-05-09; Cloud provider A regional failover of digital banking observed on 2026-05-30; Cloud provider B credit decisioning restore on 2026-06-13 took 9 hours against a 24-hour RTO

title: Risk analysis workshops
source_system: Workshops (Cyber Defense; Fraud Strategy; Payments Operations; Treasury Management; Core Banking Technology; Digital Banking Technology; Third-Party Risk Management; Integration Management Office; Model Risk Management; broker-dealer compliance; Enterprise Resilience)
owner: Director of Technology and Operational Risk
what_it_shows: Owners' accounts of past incidents, near misses and threat scenarios in their areas, and the existing controls they rely on; callbacks rely on recognizing the voices of known contacts; the mainframe team's age profile and succession concern; the core software release reaches the end of vendor support in 2028, with an upgrade planned for 2027

title: Gap analysis interviews with control owners

title: Gap analysis contract and third-party reviews
source_system: Contract management system; vendor contact register; SOC review files
what_it_shows: All 41 critical contracts: 9 have no incident notice time frame and no designated 12 CFR 53.4 contact, 5 of them inherited from the acquired bank, and those 5 also have no Florida third-party notice term; designated contacts sent to 32 of the 41 critical third parties; SOC review files for the 41: 7 late and 12 without complementary user entity control mapping; all 31 broker-dealer service provider contracts: 14, including the clearing firm, have no 72-hour notice term

title: Gap analysis samples: payments and callbacks
source_system: Treasury management platform; payments hub; callback team log; branch request records; fraud use case list
what_it_shows: 60 of 18,400 new wire beneficiaries added on the treasury platform (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30): 11 were paid under $100,000 without out-of-band confirmation, as the configuration allows; 60 of 2,940 branch-originated email or phone wire requests: 4 without callback evidence; 60 of 3,600 callback team requests: callback evidence for all; 60 of about 1.36 million outgoing wires: maker-checker recorded for all; the fraud use case list has no rule for a new beneficiary paid under $100,000 within 24 hours
